newsitem.title: CHINA: China defence industry seen entering growth period.
newsitem.headline: China defence industry seen entering growth period.

text.p: China's defence industry will enter a new period of growth over the next few years as the nation follows the latest overseas technological developments, the China Daily said on Saturday.

Beijing would rely mainly on domestic resources to develop the defence sector, the official newspaper quoted Chen Dazhi, vice minister of the State Commission for Science, Technology and Industry for National Defence, as saying.
China's military-owned industries have in recent years moved to create new revenue sources by shifting much of their production capacity toward making goods for civilian markets.
Over the past decade, civilian production by military units had grown more than 20 percent a year, and now accounted for 83 percent of total military output, the China Daily said.
About half of China's motorcycles, 30 percent of colour televisions and 10 percent of minivans were made by defence-linked enterprises, it said.
Civilian products had been exported to more than 30 countries and regions, it said but gave no details.
The military sector had boosted the creation of high-technology civilian counterparts such as commercial satellite launching, and would soon enter a new period of growth, Vice Minister Chen said.
"From 1996 to 2000, we will have an arduous task of research, production and testing," China Daily quoted him as saying but did not elaborate.
